meta.title: Frequency Lab Dataset
meta.description: Structured research database of auditory frequencies. Scientific claims are separated from traditional/spiritual claims. No claim is presented as definitive scientific fact.
meta.disclaimer: This dataset is for educational and research exploration purposes. Audio stimulation is not a medical treatment. Consult healthcare professionals for health-related decisions. Evidence levels reflect current published literature and are subject to change.

scientific.name: Scientific Frequencies
scientific.description: Frequencies investigated in peer-reviewed research related to brainwave bands, attention, relaxation, memory, sleep and cognition.

mystical.name: Mystical / Spiritual Frequencies
mystical.description: Frequencies popular in spiritual, cultural and alternative wellness traditions. Spiritual claims are clearly labeled and are not presented as scientific proof.

strong.label: Strong Evidence
strong.description: Multiple high-quality RCTs or meta-analyses with consistent findings.

moderate.label: Moderate Evidence
moderate.description: Several controlled studies or one high-quality meta-analysis with supportive findings.

limited.label: Limited Evidence
limited.description: Few studies, small samples, or mixed results.

preliminary.label: Preliminary
preliminary.description: Early-stage research, animal studies, or pilot human trials.

insufficient.label: Insufficient Evidence
insufficient.description: Very few or no rigorous studies; claims largely anecdotal.

traditional.label: Traditional / Spiritual Claim
traditional.description: Cultural, historical or spiritual tradition; not scientific evidence.

frequencies.name: Delta – Deep Sleep Band
frequencies.intendedEffect: Associated with deep, dreamless sleep and restorative processes. Investigated for sleep quality and recovery.
frequencies.humanEvidence: EEG studies consistently show delta (0.5–4 Hz) dominance during stage N3 deep sleep. Auditory entrainment attempts via binaural beats show mixed and generally limited success in shifting sleep architecture in healthy adults.
frequencies.sampleSize: Varies; many observational EEG studies; intervention trials typically n < 50
frequencies.results: Strong correlation of endogenous delta with deep sleep. Causal effect of external 2 Hz auditory stimulation on sleep stages remains weakly supported.
frequencies.safetyNotes: Low-frequency tones at moderate volume are generally safe. Avoid high volumes. Not a substitute for medical sleep treatment.
frequencies.source: Standard EEG classification (e.g., Iber et al. AASM manual); various binaural-beat sleep studies

frequencies.name: Theta – Meditation & Memory Band
frequencies.intendedEffect: Linked to relaxed, meditative, and drowsy states; hippocampal theta associated with memory encoding and creativity.
frequencies.humanEvidence: A 2024 Nature Scientific Reports study reported preliminary cognitive benefits from daily 6 Hz binaural beats. Meta-analyses of binaural beats show modest effects on anxiety and some cognitive measures, with heterogeneity.
frequencies.sampleSize: Small to moderate (e.g., n≈30–100 in individual trials)
frequencies.results: Some studies report improved relaxation or mild cognitive effects; results are not uniform across all trials.
frequencies.safetyNotes: Safe at moderate listening levels. May induce drowsiness; avoid while driving or operating machinery.
frequencies.source: Chockboondee et al., Sci Rep 2024; binaural-beat meta-analyses

frequencies.name: Alpha – Relaxed Alertness
frequencies.intendedEffect: Associated with calm, relaxed yet alert states; eyes-closed resting EEG. Explored for stress reduction and focused calm.
frequencies.humanEvidence: Alpha (≈8–12 Hz) is a robust EEG marker of relaxed wakefulness. Auditory stimulation at alpha frequencies shows mixed evidence for entrainment and subjective relaxation; some positive small trials exist.
frequencies.results: Endogenous alpha is well-established. External auditory induction of alpha shows limited-to-moderate support for subjective calm.
frequencies.safetyNotes: Generally safe. Can promote relaxation; monitor for excessive drowsiness in safety-critical contexts.
frequencies.source: Standard EEG band classification; various entrainment studies

frequencies.name: Beta – Active Focus
frequencies.intendedEffect: Associated with active thinking, concentration, and alert problem-solving. Higher beta linked to anxiety in some contexts.
frequencies.humanEvidence: Beta (≈13–30 Hz) is the dominant wake EEG band during cognitive effort. Binaural-beat studies targeting beta show inconsistent cognitive enhancement effects.
frequencies.results: Clear endogenous association with active cognition. Causal benefit of external beta stimulation remains limited and mixed.
frequencies.safetyNotes: May increase alertness or, in some individuals, feelings of tension. Use moderate volume.

frequencies.name: Gamma 40 Hz – Sensory Stimulation Research
frequencies.intendedEffect: Investigated for modulation of gamma oscillations, microglial activity, and amyloid pathology in Alzheimer's disease models and early human trials.
frequencies.humanEvidence: MIT Tsai Lab and subsequent studies (mouse + early human) show that 40 Hz sensory stimulation can entrain gamma activity and reduce amyloid pathology in models. Human trials report safety and preliminary cognitive/biomarker signals; larger confirmatory trials ongoing.
frequencies.sampleSize: Mouse studies large; human trials still relatively small (tens to low hundreds)
frequencies.results: Promising preclinical and early clinical signals for AD-related pathology and some cognitive measures. Not yet established as a clinical treatment.
frequencies.safetyNotes: Auditory 40 Hz click trains at moderate intensity are generally well-tolerated in published trials. Avoid very high volumes. Not an approved medical therapy.
frequencies.source: Murdock et al. Nature 2024; Tsai Lab publications; Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience reviews

frequencies.name: Binaural Beats (General)
frequencies.intendedEffect: Presentation of two slightly different pure tones to each ear; the brain perceives a beat frequency equal to the difference. Investigated for anxiety, attention, pain and sleep.
frequencies.humanEvidence: Meta-analyses (e.g., 2019) report positive effects on anxiety, cognition and pain perception with moderate effect sizes and notable heterogeneity. Results vary by beat frequency, duration and individual differences.
frequencies.results: Modest average benefits for anxiety reduction and some cognitive outcomes; not universal and mechanism still under study.
frequencies.safetyNotes: Requires stereo headphones. Safe at moderate volumes. Effects are typically subtle.

frequencies.name: Monaural Beats
frequencies.intendedEffect: Amplitude-modulated tone presented identically to both ears, producing a physical beat. Compared with binaural beats in some entrainment studies.
frequencies.humanEvidence: Fewer dedicated studies than binaural beats. Some research suggests monaural beats can produce stronger neural entrainment in certain frequency ranges because the modulation is physical rather than perceptual.
frequencies.results: Preliminary indications of entrainment efficacy; evidence base smaller than for binaural beats.
frequencies.safetyNotes: Can be listened to with speakers or headphones. Moderate volume recommended.

frequencies.name: Isochronic Tones
frequencies.intendedEffect: Regularly pulsed tones (on/off) at a target frequency. Claimed to produce clearer entrainment than continuous tones.
frequencies.humanEvidence: Limited peer-reviewed comparison studies. Popular in commercial brainwave products; rigorous evidence is still emerging and currently weaker than for binaural beats overall.
frequencies.results: Anecdotal and preliminary support; high-quality independent evidence remains limited.
frequencies.safetyNotes: Pulsed tones can feel more intense; start at low volume. Safe for most users at moderate levels.

frequencies.name: 396 Hz – Solfeggio
frequencies.claimedEffect: In spiritual traditions associated with liberation from guilt and fear, and root-chakra themes.
frequencies.humanEvidence: No rigorous clinical evidence that 396 Hz specifically produces unique physiological or psychological effects beyond general music listening. Origin of the specific Hz value is modern numerological (Puleo/Horowitz), not ancient documented tuning.
frequencies.studyType: None of high quality specific to this frequency
frequencies.results: Claims remain traditional/spiritual. General benefits of pleasant sound or music are well-known but not frequency-specific.
frequencies.safetyNotes: Pure tones at moderate volume are safe. No known special risk.

frequencies.name: 417 Hz – Solfeggio
frequencies.claimedEffect: Associated in spiritual contexts with facilitating change and undoing negative situations.
frequencies.humanEvidence: No controlled scientific evidence supporting unique effects of 417 Hz. Claims are cultural/spiritual.

frequencies.name: 528 Hz – 'Love Frequency' / Solfeggio
frequencies.claimedEffect: Widely claimed in alternative literature to repair DNA, promote transformation and 'love'. These extraordinary claims lack scientific support.
frequencies.humanEvidence: A small 2018 pilot (n=9) reported reduced salivary cortisol and increased oxytocin after 5 min of 528 Hz music vs 440 Hz. Animal/in-vitro work exists but does not support DNA-repair claims in humans. Reviews describe evidence as limited and low-quality. DNA-repair claims are not supported by credible biology of audible sound.
frequencies.results: Preliminary signals for stress markers in one tiny study; extraordinary healing claims unsupported.
frequencies.safetyNotes: Safe as ordinary music/tones. Do not rely on it for medical or genetic outcomes.
frequencies.source: Akimoto et al. 2018; subsequent critical reviews

frequencies.name: 639 Hz – Solfeggio
frequencies.claimedEffect: Spiritual literature associates it with harmonious relationships and heart-centered connection.
frequencies.humanEvidence: No specific controlled evidence for unique effects of 639 Hz.

frequencies.name: 741 Hz – Solfeggio
frequencies.claimedEffect: Claimed in spiritual sources to support expression, problem-solving and 'detoxification'.
frequencies.humanEvidence: No rigorous scientific evidence for frequency-specific effects.

frequencies.name: 852 Hz – Solfeggio
frequencies.claimedEffect: Associated in spiritual literature with intuition and returning to spiritual order.
frequencies.humanEvidence: No controlled evidence of unique effects.

frequencies.name: 963 Hz – Solfeggio
frequencies.claimedEffect: Often called the 'frequency of the gods' or linked to pineal activation and oneness in spiritual texts.
frequencies.humanEvidence: No scientific evidence for pineal activation or unique physiological effects of 963 Hz audible sound.
frequencies.safetyNotes: Safe at normal volumes. High pure tones can be fatiguing; use moderate levels.

frequencies.name: 432 Hz Tuning
frequencies.claimedEffect: Claimed by proponents to be more 'natural', relaxing, or cosmically aligned than the ISO standard A=440 Hz.
frequencies.humanEvidence: A small double-blind study (Calamassi & Pomponi) found modest reductions in heart rate and anxiety with 432 Hz-tuned music vs 440 Hz in dental patients. Other studies find little or no difference. The 8 Hz difference is perceptually subtle. Extraordinary 'natural harmony' claims lack robust support.
frequencies.results: Possible mild preference or relaxation difference for some listeners; not established as medically superior.
frequencies.safetyNotes: Identical safety profile to ordinary music. Preference is individual.

frequencies.name: 440 Hz – Concert Pitch (ISO)
frequencies.intendedEffect: International standard reference pitch (A4 = 440 Hz) adopted for orchestral and instrument interoperability.
frequencies.humanEvidence: ISO 16 standard. No evidence that 440 Hz is harmful or that it was imposed for nefarious reasons. It is a practical engineering convention.
frequencies.results: Widely used standard with no demonstrated health detriment relative to nearby pitches.
